newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain one pct in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain one pct in active trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares gained an average 1.09 percent in lively trade on Wednesday with the help of late activity in shares of largely state-owned firms, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a day's high of 67,673.94, up 729.16 points from Tuesday. Non-stop gains totalled 4.5 percent so far this week after last week's 2.1 percent rise.
Trade volume leapt to 10.83 trillion lira ($120.2 million) from yesterday's 9.6 trillion ($107 million).

Brokers said profit-taking was earlier sparked as the index tested the 67,500 barrier, but late activity in highly capitalised state stocks which have a major impact on the market index, produced a recovery.

"The market continued its rise with (down) corrections. Particularly, the late buying in state shares supported the rise, but we cannot say for sure that the 67,500 barrier is broken," said Sevim Ozyurt from Sumerbank.
"Trade may be squeezed at these levels tomorrow. If the rise continues with firm volume, a medium-term uptrend will be confirmed although profit-taking may occur in the short-term," she added.
